rules.statement: Do not end a session or change any other state on an HTTP GET; an RP-initiated logout endpoint takes only a form POST, and its GET answers 405.
rules.why: A GET runs on browser prefetch and can be triggered cross-site, and a GET link that carries a guard leaks it into history, server logs and the Referer header.
rules.check: Look for logout or other state-changing endpoints mapped to GET, or logout links (`<a href>`) where a `<form method="post">` is needed.

rules.statement: Guard a cookie-authenticated logout POST with a random per-session token carried in the form body. Reject the request with 400 and keep the session when the request is not a form post or the token is missing, mismatched or repeated, and ignore any copy of the token in the query string.
rules.why: Logout is a top-level navigation that can't carry the anti-forgery header, so the per-session synchronizer token prevents logout CSRF. Keeping it in the body keeps it out of URLs.
rules.check: Check that the logout handler reads the guard only from the form body, requires exactly one value, ignores query-string values and answers 400 without ending the session on failure.

rules.statement: Compare secret tokens such as anti-forgery or logout guards with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, not with `==` or `string.Equals`.
rules.why: A comparison that takes the same time whatever the input doesn't leak the guard through timing.
rules.check: Look for guard, token or secret values compared with `==`, `Equals` or `SequenceEqual`.

rules.statement: Validate a logout return URL against the configured allowlist, require it to appear at most once, and answer 400 when it fails; when it is absent, use a safe default such as `/`.
rules.why: Without that check, the logout endpoint becomes an open redirect.
rules.check: Look for a returnUrl or post_logout_redirect_uri taken from the request and used without an allowlist check, or without rejecting duplicate values.

rules.statement: Make logout idempotent: when there is no session, redirect to the return URL instead of failing.
rules.why: A second click or a stale tab should do no harm.
rules.check: Check that the logout handler doesn't return an error when the session is already gone.

rules.statement: At logout, first remove the server-side session and delete the cookie with `CancellationToken.None`. Then revoke the refresh token (RFC 7009) with `CancellationToken.None`, bounded by a timeout, and log any failure from that revocation, a cancellation included, without failing the logout.
rules.why: A client that disconnects must not leave the session behind, and the user asked to leave, so the session ends locally whatever happens at the provider.
rules.check: Look for session removal or revocation that passes the request's aborted token, revocation done before the local session is removed, or a revocation failure that fails the logout.

rules.statement: In a back-channel logout receiver, find the sessions through `sid`/`sub` indexes rather than by scanning or listing the store. Before ending a candidate session, check that it matches the token's issuer, matches its `sid` when the token has one, and belongs to the receiving client.
rules.why: Scanning doesn't scale and needs a store that can list keys. The matching checks stop one logout token from ending sessions that belong to another issuer or client.
rules.check: Look for store enumeration in the back-channel handler, or sessions ended without checking issuer, sid and client.

rules.statement: Record a logout token's `jti` as handled only after the sessions it names have ended. When handling fails, answer 400 without recording the `jti`.
rules.why: If the `jti` is recorded first, a store failure turns the provider's retry into a refused replay.
rules.check: Check the order of operations in the back-channel handler: the replay or `jti` record must come after the sessions have ended, and must not happen on an error path.

rules.statement: Require `sid` in back-channel logout tokens by default, matching the client's registered `backchannel_logout_session_required=true`. Accept `sub`-only tokens only when an explicit option turns this off.
rules.why: Otherwise one provider session could end every session the user has.
rules.check: Look for a session-required option that defaults to false, or a handler that accepts `sub`-only tokens without the option being set.

rules.statement: A back-channel logout endpoint answers 200 with `Cache-Control: no-store` on success, and 400 when the request or token is invalid, the provider's keys can't be read, or a session can't be ended.
rules.why: These are the responses OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout specifies, and a 400 makes the provider retry.
rules.check: Check the receiver's status codes and that the success response sets `Cache-Control: no-store`.
